findings.description: A boolean budget_cents_max: false bypasses the promised fail-closed handling. The yq expression `budget_cents_max // 600` replaces false with 600 before validation, leaving budget_scale: diff active.
findings.failure_mode: With budget_cents: 150, budget_scale: diff, budget_cents_max: false and an estimate of 300 cents, the gate authorizes dispatch with an effective budget of 360 cents instead of falling back to fixed and refusing.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the raw maximum and its YAML type. Default only an absent/null value; treat boolean false as malformed and select fixed scaling.

findings.description: Python multiline signatures are treated as ending the function. For `def f(\n    arg,\n):`, the closing signature line has the same indentation as the def, so close_line returns before reaching the function body.
findings.failure_mode: Body lines receive no function scope. A valid citation and planted defect in the same function, more than three lines apart, are incorrectly graded as a miss, changing recall and pass/fail results.
findings.suggested_fix: Track completion of the Python signature before applying body dedentation rules, or derive function spans with Python's AST.

findings.description: The new absence classifier recognizes only status failed as an ordinary gate error. Actual dissent envelopes also use api_failure and malformed_response, as defined by adversarial-finding.schema.json; both fall through to reason none.
findings.failure_mode: A gate that produces no usable dissent because its API request or response parsing failed is recorded as having run successfully and omitted from dissent_absent_gates, corrupting absence metrics and comparisons between arms.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify api_failure and malformed_response as error, and explicitly enumerate successful statuses before returning none.

findings.description: The new dissent_absent_reason classifier maps envelope metadata.status to a reason, but only recognises "budget_exceeded", a status naming "preflight", "failed" and recorded_by=record-fallback. The statuses the gate actually emits when the dissent produced nothing are "api_failure" and "malformed_response" (see the metadata.status enum in .claude/schemas/adversarial-finding.schema.json, touched in this diff, and the api_failure/malformed_response exits in adversarial-review.sh). Those fall through to the else branch and are reported as "none" (the dissent ran), and the gate is omitted from dissent_absent_gates.
findings.failure_mode: Every eval row whose dissenter call failed at the API or returned an unparseable payload is recorded as having had a working dissent. The report's dissent-absence accounting (the field's stated purpose) is silently wrong for exactly the failure class it was added to surface, and --validate accepts the row because "none" is an allowed value.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat status api_failure and malformed_response as "error" (e.g. `elif ($st | IN("failed","api_failure","malformed_response")) or $rb == "record-fallback" then "error"`), and update the header comment so the rule names the gate's real status values.

findings.description: Bash end-of-definition detection returns the first line after the header that starts with `}` at the header's indentation. Bash files in this corpus routinely embed heredocs (python3 - <<'PY', jq programs, JSON) whose bodies contain a `}` at column 0 inside a top-level function body. That line terminates the function's scope early; everything after it up to the next header is treated as top-level and 'has no scope', so clause (ii) same-function credit is lost for defects planted in the remainder of the function. Separately, headers() measures indentation with expandtabs(8) while close_line compares `len(t) - len(t.lstrip())` without expanding tabs, so a tab-indented nested function's closing brace never matches and its span runs to the next header.
findings.failure_mode: Defects seeded after an embedded heredoc in a long bash function are graded under ±3 only, under-crediting valid same-function citations; the grader's recall differs by file layout rather than by reviewer behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip heredoc bodies (track `<<[-]?['"]?WORD` openers until the terminator line) before testing for `}`, or require the closing brace line to be exactly `}` / `};` with nothing else, and compute both indentations with the same expandtabs(8) normalisation.

findings.description: The budget_exceeded envelope now carries metadata.reason: "budget" (and already carried status: "budget_exceeded", estimated_cents, estimate_voices). The documentation contract .claude/schemas/adversarial-finding.schema.json, edited in this same diff to add budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max, declares metadata with additionalProperties: false and a status enum that contains none of budget_exceeded, reason, estimated_cents or estimate_voices.
findings.failure_mode: Any consumer validating envelopes against the published schema rejects every budget-refused envelope; the schema update in this PR was the moment to close the gap and instead widened it with a new undeclared key.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "budget_exceeded" to metadata.status, and declare reason (enum ["budget"]), estimated_cents and estimate_voices in the metadata properties.

findings.description: budget_scale / budget_cents_effective / budget_cents_max are merged into the envelope only at one late point in main() (after model_attempts/final_model). The api_failure, malformed_response and other early-exit envelopes written between the budget gate and that line never receive them, although the header and both ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md files state that whenever the key is written 'the envelope's metadata carries' the three fields.
findings.failure_mode: ablation-row/report consumers that read budget_scale to confirm the eval config variant took effect see it absent on every failed run, indistinguishable from a config without the key.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold `$_budget_meta` into a shared envelope-emit helper (or apply `.metadata += $bm` in each early-exit jq) so every envelope written after the budget gate carries the scaling fields.

findings.description: The row writer decides the 'disabled' (planned, benign) absence reason by reading sandbox/.loa.config.yaml, which the agent under evaluation can write. ablation-grade.sh's header (touched in this diff) explicitly refuses sandbox copies as tamperable and treats eval/ copies as authoritative. 'disabled' outranks every other reason in the precedence chain, so an agent that flips flatline_protocol.enabled (or <gate>.enabled) to false converts what should be an 'error'/missing-envelope row into a planned 'disabled' row.
findings.failure_mode: A run whose agent disabled its own dissent gate is reported as an intentionally disabled arm rather than a gate failure, and dissent_absent_gates lists it as planned absence; mount_changed may flag it separately but the reason field itself is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive 'disabled' only from harness-owned evidence (meta/arm-evidence.txt lines such as dissent=false / flatline=off written by apply_arm_toggles) or from the harness-authoritative eval/ copy of the config, not from sandbox/.

findings.description: Validity is applied before the RANGE_CAP truncation: a cited range whose end exceeds the head file's line count is discarded entirely, even when its first line is valid and lies within ±3 of a site. When the head file is unavailable, the same range is capped to its first line and credited. The 1.2.0 rule (and the recall_pm3 results emitted beside it) credited such a range.
findings.failure_mode: The same review text grades differently depending on whether head/ resolved, and a reviewer citing `file:40-120` for a defect at line 41 in a 100-line file gets zero credit under the headline recall while recall_pm3 credits it; credits_function_only cannot explain the gap because it only lists additions.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the RANGE_CAP truncation (b = a when wider than 25) before the head-file bounds check, or clamp b to the file length instead of rejecting the citation outright.
